evidence.title: 鱼跃鸢飞总平面图, list card
evidence.summary: The site's card for this plan places the 鱼跃鸢飞 Yuyue Yuanfei scene just inside 大北门 Da Beimen, the Great North Gate, which it says was also called 北楼门 Beilou Men; this is the site's modern description, not a statement read on the sheet.

evidence.title: 北门 in orders of 1733-34 (see the S47 rows); yaffin 北楼门
evidence.summary: The orders call it 北门. A blog of about 2011 says 大北门 is also called 北楼门, as S05's list has it, north of 鱼跃鸢飞 on the garden axis.

evidence.title: 若帆之阁 北门 土地庙, 山神庙 (S47 section 2.8)
evidence.summary: An order of 1734 places an earth god in a small one-bay room west of the north-gate Guandi temple, and a mountain god in the fold of the hills west of the north gate. Both sit close inside the north gate of the garden.

evidence.title: 北门内 水关 小庙 (S47 section 2.7)
evidence.summary: Orders of 1733-34 speak of a rain-god shrine at the rushing water north-west of 北苑山房 inside 北门, and of 北门内水关之河北小庙: so a water gate stood just inside the north gate by then.

evidence.title: 圆明园五朝御制诗文集注 v2, editors' note on 鱼跃鸢飞
evidence.summary: Built under Yongzheng, inside the great north gate: a double-eaved tower of two floors astride a stream, five bays each way with doors on four sides, plaques on each. 畅观轩, 铺翠环流, 传妙, 多子亭 stand by it. It survived 1860 and was lost around 1900, say the editors.
